title: Values, Types, Initialization, and Streams

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: C++ is statically typed and supports value semantics. Brace initialization makes narrowing conversions visible. Use `const` for values that should not change and `auto` when the initializer makes the exact type clear, not to hide an important contract. Integer division discards a fractional part; convert an operand before division. `std::string` manages text storage safely. Stream extraction reports failure through stream state, so validate `std::cin` before using the destination value. Prefer explicit conversions and avoid C-style casts.
keyPoints: C++ is statically typed and supports value semantics.
commonMistakes: uninitialized fundamental locals have indeterminate values
const is not automatically deep for referenced objects
